answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted identity on a shared reputation graph: each agent holds a single vertex, and minting a new one requires locking a stake plus attested work history. Funding thousands of fake vertices costs more than any profit on the horizon, since each identity burns real money. Honest agents gain weight gradually through uptime and peer attestations, so a bot swarm cannot sprint to the summit of influence overnight. The ledger is the gatekeeper: sybil identities are priced out before threatening the economy, while honest agents compound real trust over time.
